related_questions.question: How long should I wait to retest for COVID after testing negative?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test negative for COVID-19 but have symptoms, retest after 48 hours. For those exposed to COVID-19, retest after 48 hours and then again 48 hours after a second negative test (total of 3 tests over 5 days). This approach helps reduce the risk of false negatives and potential spread of the virus.

list.title: Symptomatic individuals:
list.snippet: If you have symptoms of COVID-19 and test negative with an antigen test, retest in 48 hours. If the second test is also negative and symptoms persist, consider a laboratory-based molecular test or consult with a healthcare provider.

list.title: Exposed individuals:
list.snippet: If you were exposed to COVID-19 but test negative, retest after 48 hours. If that second test is also negative, retest again 48 hours later (a total of 3 tests over 5 days). This helps to catch any potential infections that might not have been detectable in the first test.

list.title: Asymptomatic individuals with no known exposure:
